nodes.question: What is the purpose of the Measuring What Matters framework in relation to traditional measures like GDP?
nodes.answer: The purpose of the framework is to track Australia’s economic and social progress holistically alongside traditional measures such as GDP.
nodes.paragraph: Since then the Australian Government has released Measuring What Matters , their first national wellbeing framework [10]. The framework is designed to be practical, allowing tracking of Australia S economic and social progress, and it is to be used holistically alongside other traditional measures (such as GDP). In the first iteration of the framework, five key themes have been identified which are: healthy a soci- ety in which people feel well and are in good physical and mental health, can access services when they need and have the information they require to take action to improve their health; secure a society where people live peacefully, feel safe, have financial security and access to housing; sustain- able a society that sustainably uses natural and financial resources, protects and repairs the environment and builds resilience to combat challenges; cohesive a society that supports connections with family, friends and the commu- nity, values diversity and promotes belonging and culture; and prosperous a society that has a dynamic, strong econ- omy, invests in people S skills and education and provides broad opportunities for employment and well-paid secure jobs.
